standard_prerequisites: Freshman's dream in characteristic p: for a p-power q, (alpha + beta)^q = alpha^q + beta^q, since the intermediate binomial coefficients are divisible by p
Any two p-powers q, q' are bounded by a common p-power q'' (for instance q q')
core_obligations: For alpha, beta purely inseparable with alpha^q, beta^{q'} in k, take a p-power q'' >= q, q'; then (alpha + beta)^{q''} = alpha^{q''} + beta^{q''} with alpha^{q''} = (alpha^q)^{q''/q} and beta^{q''} = (beta^{q'})^{q''/q'} both in k, so alpha + beta is purely inseparable
The same computation covers the difference, and the product and quotient need only (alpha beta)^{q''} = alpha^{q''} beta^{q''} (and the analogue for the quotient) with exponents in k
The set contains k and is closed under the four field operations, hence is a subextension of E/k
proof_roadmap: Close the sum and difference under a common p-power exponent via the freshman's dream
Cover the product and quotient by the multiplicative computation and conclude subextension
